results.name: lag1_response_autocorrelation
results.description: Correlation between a participant's rating on consecutive trials (pairs within the same session only); observed > null means sequential response perseveration/assimilation the trial-independent model does not produce (observed < null means alternation).

results.name: within_session_yes_drift
results.description: Yes rate on trials in the second half of each session (trial_index >= 225) minus the first half; nonzero observed vs null ~0 means participants become more (positive) or less (negative) liberal over the session, which the stationary model cannot produce.

results.name: recency_order_effect
results.description: Among non-example targets of sets with >= 2 examples, yes rate when the target is numerically closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one minus yes rate when closer to the first; observed > null means a recency effect (observed < null a primacy effect) that the order-blind model cannot produce (null ~ only stimulus-driven differences).
results.code:
# name: recency_order_effect
# description: Among non-example targets of sets with >= 2 examples, yes rate when the target is numerically closer to the last-shown example than to the first-shown one minus yes rate when closer to the first; observed > null means a recency effect (observed < null a primacy effect) that the order-blind model cannot produce (null ~ only stimulus-driven differences).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    k = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    first = ex[:, 0]
    last = ex[np.arange(len(ex)), np.maximum(k - 1, 0)]
    isex = (ex == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = (k >= 2) & ~isex
    df_, dl = np.abs(tg - first), np.abs(tg - last)
    near_last = base & (dl < df_)
    near_first = base & (df_ < dl)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    if near_last.sum() == 0 or near_first.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[near_last].mean() - r[near_first].mean())

results.name: outside_distance_decay_slope
results.description: For targets outside the examples' [min, max] range, OLS slope of rating on log(1 + distance to the nearest example); more negative observed than null means yes-responses fall off with distance from the examples more steeply than the model predicts (less negative = flatter, broader generalization).
results.code:
# name: outside_distance_decay_slope
# description: For targets outside the examples' [min, max] range, OLS slope of rating on log(1 + distance to the nearest example); more negative observed than null means yes-responses fall off with distance from the examples more steeply than the model predicts (less negative = flatter, broader generalization).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    mn, mx = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    out = (tg < mn) | (tg > mx)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(ex - tg[:, None]), axis=1)
    x = np.log1p(dist[out])
    y = df["rating"].values.astype(float)[out]
    if len(x) < 3 or x.std() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(np.cov(x, y, ddof=0)[0, 1] / x.var())

results.name: participant_yes_rate_sd
results.description: SD across participants (rows are in session order; a new participant starts where trial_index resets to 0) of each participant's overall yes rate; observed > null means people differ in response bias/generalization breadth more than the single shared-parameter model produces.

results.name: shared_ones_digit_rule_contrast
results.description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that all share one ones digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that ones digit minus yes rate for targets without it; observed > null means people pick up the "ends in d" rule more strongly than the model (observed < null means the model over-commits to the digit rule).
results.code:
# name: shared_ones_digit_rule_contrast
# description: Among sets of >= 2 examples that all share one ones digit, yes rate for non-example targets with that ones digit minus yes rate for targets without it; observed > null means people pick up the "ends in d" rule more strongly than the model (observed < null means the model over-commits to the digit rule).
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    k = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    d = np.mod(ex, 10)
    d0 = d[:, 0]
    same = np.all(np.isnan(d) | (d == d0[:, None]), axis=1) & (k >= 2)
    isex = (ex == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    base = same & ~isex
    match = base & (np.mod(tg, 10) == d0)
    nomatch = base & (np.mod(tg, 10) != d0)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    if match.sum() == 0 or nomatch.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[match].mean() - r[nomatch].mean())

results.name: yes_rate_target_is_example
results.description: Yes rate on trials where the target is itself one of the shown examples; observed > null means people endorse already-seen examples more reliably than the model's noisy-example/tempered posterior predicts (observed < null means less).

results.name: hull_inside_minus_outside
results.description: Among non-example targets of sets with >= 2 examples, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' [min, max] range minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed > null means people generalize by magnitude range (interpolation) more sharply than the model, observed < null means less.
results.code:
# name: hull_inside_minus_outside
# description: Among non-example targets of sets with >= 2 examples, yes rate for targets strictly inside the examples' [min, max] range minus yes rate for targets outside it; observed > null means people generalize by magnitude range (interpolation) more sharply than the model, observed < null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").values
    tg = df["target"].astype(int).values.astype(float)
    k = (~np.isnan(ex)).sum(axis=1)
    mn, mx = np.nanmin(ex, axis=1), np.nanmax(ex, axis=1)
    isex = (ex == tg[:, None]).any(axis=1)
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    base = (k >= 2) & ~isex
    inside = base & (tg > mn) & (tg < mx)
    outside = base & ((tg < mn) | (tg > mx))
    if inside.sum() == 0 or outside.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[inside].mean() - r[outside].mean())
